title: He was already slipping.
paragraphs: He was already slipping.

Fingers losing grip.
Breath breaking.
Storm screaming louder than his faith.
And still… he reached.

That image isn’t just drama.
It’s you.
Because nobody talks about this part of Christianity.

The part where you’re saved…
but still fighting not to fall.

The part where you love Jesus…
but your hands are tired.

The part where your prayers feel weak,
your past feels loud,
and your future feels uncertain.
Listen carefully—

Jesus did not say,
“The one who starts strong will be saved.”
He said:

“But the one who endures to the end will be saved.”
— Matthew 24:13

That word endures is not passive.
It is violent faith.

It is choosing Christ when your flesh wants escape.
It is holding on when everything in you whispers, “Let go.”
Endurance is not pretty.

It looks like tears on your pillow.
It looks like deleted messages you wanted to send.
It looks like walking away when nobody would have known.
It looks like praying with a shaking voice.

It looks like that man in the image—
bloody, soaked, exhausted…
but still reaching.
Why?
Because something in him knows:
If he lets go—he loses everything.
But here’s the twist.
The Gospel flips the whole scene.
You think you’re the one holding on to Jesus.
But Scripture reveals something deeper:
He is holding on to you.

John 10:28 —
“No one will snatch them out of My hand.”
You see that hand reaching forward in the storm?
That’s not just desperation.
That’s grace in motion.

Because endurance is not about perfect strength—
it’s about persistent surrender.
Let’s be real.
Some of you almost gave up this week.

You smiled in public…
but battled in private.

You almost returned to that sin.
You almost quit praying.
You almost believed the lie that you’re too far gone.
But you didn’t.
You’re still here.
Still reading.
Still breathing.
Still reaching.
And heaven sees that.

Not your perfection—
your persistence.

Because real faith doesn’t say,
“I never fall.”

Real faith says,
“I keep getting back up… because Jesus is worth it.”

Some scholars interpret Matthew 24:13 as a call to remain faithful through persecution and deception in the last days. Others emphasize that endurance is the evidence of genuine saving faith—not the cause of it.
Both truths point to one Person:
Jesus Christ.

The One who endured the cross
when you couldn’t endure your sin.

The One who didn’t let go
even when it cost Him everything.
The nails didn’t make Him stay.
Love did.

So when you feel like you’re at the edge—
when your grip is weak,
your strength is gone,
and your faith feels like a thread—
Remember this:
You are not saved because you hold perfectly.
You are saved because He held nothing back.

And the same Savior who died for you
is the same Savior who keeps you.
So endure.

Not to earn His love.
But because you already have it.

Cling to Him in the storm.
Cry if you must.
Rest if you need.
Repent when you fall.
Return again and again.

Because the end is not written by your weakness—
it is secured by His victory.
And one day…

The storm will stop.
The grip will no longer strain.
Faith will become sight.
And the One you’ve been holding onto—
will be standing right in front of you.
So don’t let go.

Not now.
Not here.
Not after everything He’s done.
And comment this:

Because your quiet endurance
might be the lifeline someone else needs.
